n_status.exact: raw row count equals Woike's n with no reduction
n_status.explained: raw count differs; a stated, measured reduction (or a documented misprint) yields Woike's n AND his split
n_status.unexplained: raw count differs and no tested rule reproduces Woike's n with his split

split_status.exact: natively binary class column; raw counts equal n1/n0
split_status.exact_after_reduction: natively binary class column; counts equal n1/n0 after the explained row reduction
split_status.reproduced_by_rule: criterion needs a binarization (merging classes or thresholding a number); the stated rule reproduces n1/n0. The rule is a finding, not a decision

datasets.raw_attribute_note: 13 fields per record (line 50 has a stray leading comma, hence 14). echocardiogram.names says attributes 10-12 (mult, name, group) are to be ignored and 1, 2 and 13 (survival, still-alive, alive-at-1) carry the outcome; that leaves seven clinical attributes (3-9), of which pericardial-effusion is binary: the 1 + 6 profile of Tabelle 6.9.
datasets.criterion: Survival for at least 12 months after the heart attack. The raw file ships a derived column alive-at-1 (attribute 13) that is '?' for 57 of the 131 well-formed rows.

comparison.explanation: 132 raw lines. Rows with alive-at-1 known AND attributes 3-9 complete: 62, with alive-at-1 = 1 for 18 and 0 for 44, which is Woike's n and split exactly. CAUTION, measured on these 62 rows: the shipped alive-at-1 column does not follow its own definition in echocardiogram.names (1 = alive at one year). Of the 44 rows coded 0, 42 have survival >= 12 months (38 died later, 4 still alive) and 2 died within 12 months; of the 18 rows coded 1, 17 are still alive but were followed for fewer than 12 months (the names file says such patients cannot be used) and 1 has survival missing. Woike's 18/44 matches the column as shipped, not a re-derivation from survival and still-alive (which gives 42 survived, 2 died, 18 undeterminable).

decisions_needed: Row policy: 62 complete cases versus all rows with a determinable criterion.
Criterion: alive-at-1 as shipped (matches Woike, but contradicts the names-file definition on these rows) or a re-derivation from survival and still-alive.
Line 50 is malformed (leading comma, nearly all '?').
Cue set: the seven attributes 3-9, per the names file.

comparison.explanation: 90 raw rows (A 64, S 24, I 2; line 4 carries the token 'A ' with a trailing space, counted here as A). Three rows have '?' in COMFORT (two A, one I); 87 are complete. Removing the one remaining class-I row gives 86 = S 24 / A 62, Woike's n and split. Merging I into either class cannot give 24/62 on the complete rows (it would be 87).

decisions_needed: Class I (2 rows): drop or merge.
Three rows with '?' in COMFORT.
Positive class: Tabelle 6.9 has n1 = 24 (S); Woike et al. (2017) Table 1 reports base rate .721 (A, 'keep patient in hospital').

datasets.raw_attribute_note: 28 whitespace-separated fields. Woike used 6 cues (1 binary, 1 categorical, 4 continuous); which six is not stated, and the dissertation has no descriptive paragraph for this set.
datasets.criterion: Not described in the dissertation. Woike et al. (2017) Table 1: 'Treated with surgery (yes/no)', base rate .587 = 128/218, which points to attribute 1 (surgery: 1 = yes, 2 = no). Holte's class for the same file is attribute 24 (surgical lesion).

comparison.explanation: 300 + 68 = 368 raw rows; attribute 1: 214 yes, 152 no, 2 '?'. Woike's 218 (128/90) was NOT reproduced. Checked, for the criteria surgery (attr 1), outcome lived/not (attr 23) and surgical lesion (attr 24), on data+test, data only and test only: (a) complete cases on 4 of the 7 continuous attributes plus any two other attributes: no combination gives 218 with 128/90; (b) complete cases on ANY six of the 23 usable attributes (100,947 subsets per criterion and scope): 218 rows with a 128/90 split occur for 4 subsets with surgery on data+test (all built on attributes {6, 9, 10, 12, 20}), 5 with surgical lesion on data+test, 4 with surgery and 1 with surgical lesion on data only, none with outcome. Not one of these 14 subsets contains four continuous attributes, so none has Woike's 1/1/4 profile, and with this many subsets chance hits are expected. They are recorded as candidates, not as an explanation.

decisions_needed: Everything: criterion column, row policy, cue subset, pooling of .data and .test. Needs Woike's file or his recollection.

datasets.raw_attribute_note: 17 fields: party first, then 16 votes (y / n / ?). Sixteen predictors; Woike types all 16 as categorical, which suggests '?' was kept as a third value.
datasets.criterion: Party: democrat or republican; natively binary.

comparison.explanation: 435 raw rows (democrat 267, republican 168). Woike's 402 (248/154), i.e. 33 rows fewer (19 democrats, 14 republicans), was NOT reproduced. Checked: complete cases = 232; keeping rows with at most k '?' gives 399 (k = 2) and 415 (k = 3), never 402, also when up to two attributes are left out of the count (n = 402 occurs but never with 248/154); removing duplicate rows gives 342; the first or last 402 rows give 249/153 and 245/157. Complete cases on small attribute subsets do hit 402 with 248/154 (e.g. attributes {11, 14}, {3, 5, 8}, {6, 8, 14}), but Woike used all 16 votes and several subsets hit by chance, so none is an explanation.

decisions_needed: Row policy: Woike's 402 is unexplained; the full 435 is the defensible default.
'?' as a third category versus missing.

datasets.raw_attribute_note: 6 integer fields per data line (lines 87-586 of the text file): sex, DVRT, educational level, Leaving Certificate, father's occupational prestige, type of school. Woike names his four cues: school type, test score, sex, father's prestige.
datasets.criterion: Leaving Certificate taken (2) or not (1); natively binary.

comparison.explanation: 500 raw rows (not taken 278, taken 222). The file's own header says the simplified 441-case form removes primary terminal leavers and cases with missing data. Measured: dropping educational level 1 (37 primary terminal leavers = school type 9), educational level 0 (6 rows; an undocumented code, evidently missing) and prestige 0 (26 rows; documented as missing) leaves 435 rows, taken 211 / not taken 224 = Woike's n and split exactly. (Without the six level-0 rows it is 441 = 211/230.)

decisions_needed: Row policy: primary terminal leavers and zero-coded missing values.
Educational level must not be a cue (it determines the criterion).

datasets.raw_attribute_note: hbiostat file: 32 columns (row index + 31 variables; several renamed and recoded, posECG/equivecg merged into ecg). Original UCLA file: 42 columns. Woike used 8 cues (1 binary, 7 continuous) per Tabelle 6.9 but 5 in his results tables; none is named.
datasets.criterion: Any cardiac event within a year (MI, PTCA, CABG or death). In the ORIGINAL UCLA coding 0 = yes; hbiostat recoded to 1 = yes.

comparison.explanation: 558 rows in both files. hbiostat any.event: 1 (event) 89, 0 (no event) 469. Original UCLA 'any event': 0 (= yes, event) 89, 1 (no event) 469. NB Tabelle 6.9's n1 = 469 equals the count of raw code 1, which the UCLA codebook defines as NO event; Woike et al. (2017) label the same .841 base rate 'Heart disease'. Whether this is a labelling slip or a coding choice is for the authors.

decisions_needed: Which file: the archived original (what Woike downloaded in 2007) or the recoded hbiostat copy.
Polarity of the criterion (see comparison).
Cue subset: 8 (or 5) of about 30.
newMI, newPTCA, newCABG and death are components of the criterion and cannot be cues.

datasets.raw_attribute_note: 8 fields per game (h/a, favorite points, underdog points, point spread, favorite, underdog, year, week) plus 0-2 optional indicator tokens (night/Monday/overtime). Woike used 4 cues (1 binary, 3 continuous); not named. The two points columns define the criterion and cannot be cues.
datasets.criterion: Woike's TEXT: whether the home team wins. Derived from the two points columns; not a column of the file.

comparison.explanation: 672 games. Home team wins 391, does not win 281 (one tie): this is NOT Woike's split. Favorite wins 451, does not win 221: this IS Woike's 451/221 exactly. So the counts in Tabelle 6.9 correspond to 'favorite wins', not to 'home team wins' as the dissertation text says.

decisions_needed: Criterion: 'favorite wins' (matches Woike's numbers) or 'home team wins' (matches his words).
The single tie.
Cue subset: 4 (spread, h/a, year, week are the only non-outcome numeric fields).
